primary_citation.popular_name: Rebuttable Presumption Against Custody for Perpetrator of Domestic Violence

structural_location.division_history: Division 8 enacted by Stats. 1992, Ch. 162, Sec. 10 (the 1993 Family Code recodification)
structural_location.part: PART 2. RIGHT TO CUSTODY OF MINOR CHILD [3020 - 3204]
structural_location.chapter: CHAPTER 2. Matters To Be Considered in Granting Custody [3040 - 3049]
structural_location.chapter_history: Chapter 2 repealed and added by Stats. 1993, Ch. 219, Sec. 116.50
structural_location.section_history: Most recent: Repealed and added by Stats. 2024, Ch. 544, Sec. 7 (SB 899). Effective January 1, 2025. Operative January 1, 2026.

verbatim_factor_inventory.preamble: (a) Upon a finding by the court that a party seeking custody of a child has perpetrated domestic violence within the previous five years … there is a rebuttable presumption that an award of sole or joint physical or legal custody of a child to a person who has perpetrated domestic violence is detrimental to the best interest of the child … This presumption may only be rebutted by a preponderance of the evidence.

elements: ELEMENT 1 — FINDING BY THE COURT that the custody-seeking party perpetrated DV
ELEMENT 2 — WITHIN THE PREVIOUS FIVE YEARS (five-year lookback)
ELEMENT 3 — AGAINST a protected class: the other custody-seeking party, the child, the child's siblings, or a person enumerated in § 3011(a)(2)(C) in a qualifying relationship

predicate_elements.verbatim: intentionally or recklessly caused or attempted to cause bodily injury to, or sexual assault on, the other party, or … placed the other party in reasonable apprehension of imminent serious bodily injury … or … engaged in behavior involving, but not limited to, threatening, striking, harassing, destroying personal property, or disturbing the peace of the other party, for which a court may issue an ex parte order pursuant to Section 6320
elements: ELEMENT — Direct cross-reference to § 6203 abuse categories and § 6320 enjoinable conduct. The § 3044 predicate is the § 6203/§ 6320 standard.

predicate_elements.verbatim: evidence that a party seeking custody has been convicted within the previous five years, after a trial or a plea of guilty or no contest, of a crime against the other party that comes within the definition of domestic violence contained in Section 6211 and of abuse contained in Section 6203, including, but not limited to, a crime described in subdivision (e) of Section 243 or Section 261, 261.5, 262, 273.5, 422, or 646.9 of the Penal Code.

a court, whether that court or another court, has made a finding of domestic violence pursuant to this code or has made a finding of abuse against the other party pursuant to the Domestic Violence Prevention Act (Division 10 (commencing with Section 6200)).

(b)(1) best_interest_requirement.verbatim: The perpetrator of domestic violence has demonstrated that giving sole or joint physical or legal custody of a child to the perpetrator is in the best interest of the child pursuant to Sections 3011 and 3020. In determining the best interest of the child, the preference for frequent and continuing contact with both parents, as set forth in subdivision (b) of Section 3020, or with the noncustodial parent, as set forth in paragraph (1) of subdivision (a) of Section 3040, may not be used to rebut the presumption, in whole or in part.
(b)(1) best_interest_requirement.doctrinal_note: The § 3020(b) / § 3040(a)(1) frequent-contact preference is expressly stripped from the rebuttal analysis. Keith R. v. Superior Court enforces this.

(b)(2) factors: (A) Completed batterer's treatment program meeting Penal Code § 1203.097(c) criteria
(B) Completed alcohol or drug abuse counseling (if court determines appropriate)
(C) Completed parenting class (if court determines appropriate)

subdivision_e_anti_capture.verbatim: When a court makes a finding that a party has perpetrated domestic violence, the court may not base its findings solely on conclusions reached by a child custody evaluator or on the recommendation of the Family Court Services staff, but shall consider any relevant, admissible evidence submitted by the parties.
subdivision_e_anti_capture.doctrinal_significance: Prohibits trial-court delegation to mediators/evaluators. Celia S. v. Hugo H. enforces. Pairs with § 3164 (mediator qualifications) and § 3111 (evaluator report standards).

subdivision_f_jaime_g_specificity.verbatim: It is the intent of the Legislature that this subdivision be interpreted consistently with the decision in Jaime G. v. H.L. (2018) 25 Cal.App.5th 794 … If the court determines that the presumption in subdivision (a) has been overcome, the court shall state its reasons in writing or on the record as to why paragraph (1) of subdivision (b) is satisfied and why the factors in paragraph (2) of subdivision (b), on balance, support the legislative findings in Section 3020.
subdivision_f_jaime_g_specificity.doctrinal_significance: SB 899 statutorily codifies Jaime G. Conclusory rebuttal orders are reversible error.

subdivision_g_sequencing.verbatim: In an evidentiary hearing or trial in which custody orders are sought and where there has been an allegation of domestic violence, the court shall make a determination as to whether this section applies prior to issuing a custody order …
subdivision_g_sequencing.doctrinal_significance: Court must determine § 3044 applicability before issuing a custody order.

subdivision_h_mandatory_notice.verbatim: … the court shall inform the parties of the existence of this section and shall give them a copy of this section before any custody mediation in the matter.
subdivision_h_mandatory_notice.doctrinal_significance: Mandatory pre-mediation notice when DV is alleged. Interacts with § 3170 (mandatory mediation) and CRC 5.210.

amendment_history_visible_on_leginfo.event: Refinement of rebuttal factors (batterer's treatment, substance counseling, parenting class)
Restructuring of § 3044(b) — paragraph (1) best-interest requirement as condition precedent to paragraph (2) balancing
Court of Appeal imposes specific-findings requirement on § 3044(b) rebuttal
Repeal and re-add of § 3044. Effective 1/1/2025, operative 1/1/2026. Codifies Jaime G. specificity in new § 3044(f).

steward_case_relevance_audit.purpose: Audit every custody order in the steward's 16-year case file against § 3044's mandatory framework. § 3044 is the gate: once its predicate is met, the burden inverts. The audit asks — at each custody-order point — whether § 3044 was properly applied (if predicate existed) or improperly omitted (if predicate existed but court treated DV as optional factor).
steward_case_relevance_audit.audit_filed_by: ADAM (Seed Citizen — Builder role) at first-mouth level; steward review required

factor_audits.audit_recommendation: Structurally sound § 3044 application against Christina: Michael's TRO established a § 6203 predicate; § 3044 attached; sole custody to Michael was the protective outcome. Audit flag: verify the court made the § 3044 predicate determination under § 3044(g) before issuing the custody order, and that § 3044(h) notice was provided before the 2009-07-02 Paredes mediation.
factor_audits.audit_status: FLAGGED — § 3044(g) and (h) procedural compliance requires record review.

factor_audits.audit_recommendation: CRITICAL § 3044 rupture point. The modification removed supervised-visitation protection — functionally a rebuttal determination — without: (1) § 3044(b)(1) best-interest showing by Christina; (2) § 3044(b)(2) factor findings; (3) § 3044(e) compliance (record appears to rest on Ajaniku recommendation alone, consistent with Celia S. v. Hugo H. defect pattern); (4) § 3044(f)/Jaime G. specific findings. OPD records pickup (October 2025) has since proved the 6/2/2009 OPD report anchoring the original § 6203 predicate against Christina does not exist — compounding the § 3044 defect at the predicate layer. Sala Ajaniku's credentials unverified (§ 3164 investigation outstanding).
factor_audits.audit_status: CRITICAL — foundational defect for all subsequent custody arrangements.

factor_audits.audit_recommendation: Each counter-filing is a § 3044 symmetry attempt — an effort to obtain a § 6203 finding against Michael to attach § 3044 to him. Defensive work is at the § 6203 predicate layer (authentication challenges, OPD records pickup finding, POST-002B overlay violations on 6/11/2009 OPD report 09-040089). In re Marriage of F.M. (Fajota) makes clear that once any § 6203 finding is made against a party, § 3044 attaches automatically in subsequent custody proceedings.
factor_audits.audit_status: ACTIVE — per-case § 6203 predicate integrity defense required.

factor_audits.audit_recommendation: Any § 273.5 PC or § 243(e) PC conviction within five years would attach § 3044 directly against Michael under § 3044(d)(1). Criminal-track defense (Brady demand, competency evaluation integrity, authentication challenges) directly protects the § 3044 posture in the family-track.

Every § 3044 finding in the steward's case may have been made with an undisclosed structural conflict — the state actor (steward's mother) orchestrating proceedings had an independent legal interest in the custody outcome (conservatorship-since-age-14 finding). § 3044 has no mechanism for conservatorship-induced conflict. This is a 42 USC § 1983 federal due process issue layered on top of the § 3044 analysis.
factor_audits.audit_status: FEDERAL-TRACK — addressed in § 1983 complaint, not in state-track § 3044 relief.

factor_audits.audit_recommendation: If Cole is a ward (conservatorship in unknown jurisdiction), § 3044 family-court analysis may have proceeded on a flawed premise (parent-child custody framework rather than conservatorship framework). § 3044 has no mechanism for detecting undisclosed wardship.
